findings.title: Failed 'Add entry' wipes the text the user typed
findings.where: Plant detail page /plants/:id, Journal > New entry (pages/plants/[id].vue addEntry)
findings.steps: Open a plant, type a journal entry, make the POST /api/journal fail (server down, network error, 422/500) and click Add entry.
findings.expected: The error is shown and the typed text stays in the textarea so the user can retry.
findings.actual: addEntry calls entryForm.reset() inside `finally`, so the body is cleared on failure as well as on success. The error message shows but the user's text is gone.
findings.evidence: Code: `finally { addingEntry.value = false; entryForm.value?.reset(); entryForm.value?.focus() }`. reset() sets form.body = ''. The component comment even says reset is for 'after a successful save'.

findings.title: Journal body containing a NUL character causes a 500
findings.steps: POST {"plant_id":1,"entry_on":"2026-11-01","body":"\u0000abc"}, or PUT the same body to /api/journal/1.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error. SQLite's length() stops at NUL, so the CHECK constraint fails and the IntegrityError is not handled.
findings.evidence: curl returned 'Internal Server Error 500' for both the POST and the PUT.

findings.title: Out-of-range IDs cause 500s on the journal endpoints
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow). No upper bound is validated.
findings.evidence: All three requests returned 500 via curl.

findings.title: Character limit counts UTF-16 units, so emoji entries are limited to half and existing entries can't be edited
findings.steps: Type emoji in the entry textarea, or edit an entry the server accepted with 300 emoji (created through the API, which counts code points).
findings.expected: The client and server agree on the 500-character limit.
findings.actual: The textarea maxlength and the .length checks count UTF-16 code units, so only 250 emoji fit. Editing a 300-emoji entry (which the server accepts) shows '-100 characters left' and blocks Save with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.'
findings.evidence: The API accepted a 300-emoji body (201). The frontend uses form.body.length and maxlength=500.

findings.title: Searching for more than 80 characters shows a raw validation error and no results
findings.steps: Type or paste a search term longer than 80 characters.
findings.expected: The input limits its length, or the search handles long text gracefully.
findings.actual: The API returns 422 and the page shows 'Q: String should have at most 80 characters' in place of the list. The input has no maxlength.
findings.evidence: GET /api/journal?q=<81 chars> returned 422 with string_too_long on query.q.

findings.title: Journal load errors have no retry
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section on /plants/:id
findings.steps: Load the page while the API is failing, then bring the API back.
findings.expected: The error state offers a Retry button that reloads the data.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown, with no retry control. The user has to reload the page or change the search.
findings.evidence: journal.vue and [id].vue render AlertMessage for loadError/journalLoadError without any button calling refresh.

findings.title: No request timeouts; a hung API leaves 'Saving…' and 'Loading entries…' indefinitely
findings.steps: Make the API hang without responding, then add, edit or delete an entry, or search.
findings.expected: Requests fail after 10 seconds with a visible error and the buttons are re-enabled.
findings.actual: No timeout is configured on $fetch, so the buttons stay disabled and the page shows 'Saving…' or 'Loading entries…' until the browser gives up.
findings.evidence: No `timeout` option in useApiClient or in the journal calls.

findings.title: Retrying an add after a timeout or network error creates duplicate entries
findings.steps: Submit an entry, lose the response (timeout or network drop after the server commits), then click Add entry again.
findings.actual: The POST has no idempotency key or duplicate guard, so a retry creates a second identical entry. A retried delete shows 'Journal entry not found.' as an error even though the delete succeeded.
findings.evidence: create_entry inserts unconditionally. A second DELETE of the same id returned 404.

findings.title: Long plant names in the Journal feed can overflow at 375px
findings.steps: Give a plant a long name with no spaces (e.g. 60 characters) and open /journal at 375px wide.
findings.actual: The link has no overflow-wrap (only the body has overflow-wrap:anywhere), so the head row can scroll sideways.
findings.evidence: CSS: .journal-feed__plant has no overflow-wrap or word-break.
